interpretation: Metadata scoring over existing candidates is the strongest measured improvement target. candidate_accumulation_ms currently starts immediately before metadata_ms and both stop after the metadata loop, so these values overlap and must not be added. The loop materializes candidate IDs and then relooks up each candidate with HashMap::entry; iterating candidates mutably can remove that Vec allocation and redundant map access. A further breakdown is needed before changing topic, doc-type, or claim scoring.

candidate_metadata_iteration_experiment.change: Iterate candidates.iter_mut() directly instead of collecting candidate IDs into a Vec and re-looking up each entry.
candidate_metadata_iteration_experiment.assessment: The metadata loop timing fell from 0.416 ms to 0.391 ms median. End-to-end throughput was mixed: C1 increased slightly while C10 decreased in this three-run sample. Treat the throughput result as inconclusive; the change removes one temporary candidate-ID vector and a redundant candidate-map lookup per candidate, but has not demonstrated a reliable throughput gain.

metadata_substage_profile.sampling: One candidate in every 64 was timed for each substage; 660 timing rows across three repetitions.
metadata_substage_profile.interpretation: Candidate resolution (doc_u32_to_id and docs lookups) was the largest sampled substage, followed by topic scoring; document-type and claim scoring were smaller. These are sampled directional timings, not CPU percentages. Per-stage estimates do not sum cleanly to metadata_ms because sampled timers add overhead and are aggregated separately.
metadata_substage_profile.note: Throughput in this profile includes metadata substage sampling overhead and should not be compared to uninstrumented runs.
